headers.//: Images are content-hashed by the build — the name changes when the bytes do — so a browser never needs to ask about one twice.

The stamp a running page polls to notice it has been replaced. Cached, it would advertise the build it was deployed alongside for as long as the CDN felt like it, and no open tab would ever hear about a deploy.
Likewise the worker itself, and the pages it caches: they carry the build id, so they have to come from the network to change.
